skill.name: caveman-commit
skill.description: Generates terse Conventional Commit messages that preserve intent, context, and required change notes.
skill.summary: Create concise Conventional Commit messages from change context.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code and fenced commit message examples in SKILL.md. I found no evidence of external command execution, prompt injection, network access, secret handling, or filesystem modification intent.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 15 uses markdown inline code to describe the Conventional Commit subject format. It is documentation text and does not instruct the agent to execute a shell command.
Line 16 lists allowed commit types inside markdown backticks. These are literal labels for commit formatting, not executable commands.
Line 26 uses markdown inline code to show the preferred bullet character. This is formatting guidance with no command execution behavior.
Line 27 uses markdown inline code for issue and pull request trailer examples. The text is commit message guidance, not shell execution.
Lines 41-48 are a fenced markdown example of the expected commit message output. The block contains plain commit message text, not instructions to run commands.
Lines 48-52 are markdown fence delimiters around documentation examples. They do not create execution behavior or command invocation.
Lines 52-57 show a fenced example for a breaking-change commit message. The content is static documentation, not a shell command or script.
Lines 57-65 include the example fence ending and explicitly state the skill does not run git commit. The backticks are markdown formatting, not execution.

content.value_statement: Verbose commits hide the reason for a change and slow review. This skill creates short Conventional Commit messages with context only when needed.
actual_capabilities: Generates Conventional Commit subject lines with optional scopes.
Keeps subjects short, imperative, and free of trailing periods.
Adds body text for breaking changes, migrations, reversions, and security fixes.
Uses issue and pull request references when they are provided.
Avoids AI attribution, first-person language, emoji, and redundant file names.
limitations: Requires enough change context to infer the intent accurately.
Does not stage files, run git commit, amend commits, or modify the repository.
Does not verify issue numbers or release dates against external systems.
May need adjustment for projects that do not use Conventional Commits.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Commits
use_cases.description: Turn a feature diff summary into a short commit subject and optional body.

use_cases.title: Document Risky Changes
use_cases.description: Add clear context for breaking changes, security fixes, migrations, and reversions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team History
use_cases.description: Keep commit messages consistent across reviews, branches, and release preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a concise Conventional Commit message for these changes: [describe the change].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a short change summary.

prompt_templates.title: Use Diff Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a commit message from this diff summary. Include a body only if the reason is not obvious: [paste summary].
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer has a diff summary and wants a paste-ready message.

prompt_templates.title: Include Issue Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Conventional Commit message for [change]. Reference [issue or PR] at the end when appropriate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Commit should include a tracker reference.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Breaking Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit message for this breaking change: [old behavior], [new behavior], [migration deadline], [reason].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs a body and breaking-change note.

output_examples.input: A bug fix makes expired sessions refresh correctly.
An API route was renamed and clients must migrate before a release date.
output_examples.output: feat(api)!: rename checkout route, with a breaking-change note and migration deadline.

output_examples.input: Documentation adds setup steps for local development.

best_practices: Provide the change summary, affected area, and reason when asking for a commit message.
Mention breaking changes, migrations, security fixes, and reversions explicitly.
Check the generated type and scope against the repository convention before committing.
anti_patterns: Do not request a subject-only message for breaking changes or security fixes.
Do not provide vague context such as miscellaneous updates or cleanup.
Do not keep AI attribution, marketing language, or redundant file names in the final message.

faq.question: Does this skill run git commands?
faq.answer: No. It only generates commit message text and does not stage, commit, amend, or modify files.

faq.question: Does it require Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed around Conventional Commit types, scopes, subjects, and body rules.

faq.question: When will it add a body?
faq.answer: It adds a body for non-obvious reasons, breaking changes, migrations, linked issues, reversions, and security fixes.

faq.question: Can it include issue references?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the issue or pull request number, and it can add references at the end.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a diff summary, changed area, reason for the change, and any release or migration notes.
